title: Your Credit Score Sets Your Car Insurance — $2,300 Gap
hook: Your credit score doesn't just affect loans — in 47 states, it secretly sets your car insurance rate, and the gap between poor and excellent is nearly $1,000 a year.
angle: Most people never connect credit scores to insurance costs — but insurers in 47 states legally price your premium based on a credit-based insurance score, creating a gap up to $999/year that punishes people who already have less
audience: Anyone who pays car insurance and has a credit score under 750 — especially renters and younger earners who don't know the connection exists
key_numbers: Poor credit: avg $1,867/year premium vs. excellent credit: $868/year
$999 annual gap — nearly $10,000 over ten years
42% of drivers didn't know their credit affects their insurance premium
Paying credit card balance below 10% utilization can move a tier in 30 days
